draft.title: Cyclic quadrilaterals
card: A cyclic quadrilateral is a four-sided shape with all four vertices on a circle.
Its opposite angles add to \(180^{\circ}\). So the two angles at one pair of opposite corners are supplementary, and so are the other two.
Example: in cyclic quadrilateral \(ABCD\), angle \(A = 70^{\circ}\). Angle \(C\) is opposite \(A\), so \(C = 180^{\circ} - 70^{\circ} = 110^{\circ}\).
Only opposite angles pair up. Angles at neighbouring corners, such as \(A\) and \(B\), do not have to add to \(180^{\circ}\).
draft.remember: In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles add to \(180^{\circ}\).

a.q: \(PQRS\) is a cyclic quadrilateral. Angle \(P = 85^{\circ}\). What is angle \(R\), opposite \(P\)?
a.why: Opposite angles add to \(180^{\circ}\), so \(R = 180^{\circ} - 85^{\circ} = 95^{\circ}\). Choosing \(85^{\circ}\) wrongly treats opposite angles as equal.
a.clue: Opposite angles add to a straight angle.

b.q: \(ABCD\) is a cyclic quadrilateral. Angle \(A = 2x\) and the opposite angle \(C = x + 30^{\circ}\). What is angle \(A\)?
b.why: Opposite angles add to \(180^{\circ}\), so \(2x + x + 30^{\circ} = 180^{\circ}\). Then \(3x = 150^{\circ}\) and \(x = 50^{\circ}\), so \(A = 100^{\circ}\). The option \(50^{\circ}\) is only the value of \(x\), not angle \(A\).
b.clue: Add the two opposite angles and set the sum to \(180^{\circ}\).

wants.brief: A circle with a quadrilateral ABCD drawn inside it, all four vertices A, B, C and D on the circle. Angles at A and C (opposite corners) are marked with arcs and labelled A and C.
wants.why: It shows what a cyclic quadrilateral looks like and which angles are opposite.

flags: Question b: the checker picked “\(100^{\circ}\)”, not the writer’s answer “\(110^{\circ}\)”.

Only opposite angles pair up. Angles at neighbouring vertices, such as \(A\) and \(B\), do not have to add to \(180^{\circ}\).
proposal.remember: In a cyclic quadrilateral, each pair of opposite angles is supplementary.

a.q: \(PQRS\) is a cyclic quadrilateral. Angle \(P = 85^{\circ}\). What is angle \(R\), opposite \(P\)?

a.clue: Opposite angles add to a straight angle.

b.q: \(ABCD\) is a cyclic quadrilateral. Angle \(A = 2x\) and the opposite angle \(C = x + 30^{\circ}\). What is angle \(A\)?
b.why: Opposite angles add to \(180^{\circ}\), so \(2x + x + 30^{\circ} = 180^{\circ}\). Then \(3x = 150^{\circ}\) and \(x = 50^{\circ}\), so \(A = 2 \times 50^{\circ} = 100^{\circ}\). The option \(50^{\circ}\) is only the value of \(x\), and \(80^{\circ}\) is angle \(C\), not angle \(A\).
b.clue: Add the two opposite angles and set the sum to \(180^{\circ}\).
